1: Depth-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Reconstruction of Dense Brain MRI Volumes from Sparse Slices
2: Demonstrated scope: retrospective sparse-slice FLAIR MRI reconstruction research prototype. MRI means magnetic resonance imaging; FLAIR means fluid-attenuated inversion recovery. Problem: sparse axial sampling leaves missing planes. Solution: bounding acquired slices and depth coordinates condition a two-dimensional latent denoising model, whose generated planes are assembled with the acquired planes. VAE means variational autoencoder; DDIM means denoising diffusion implicit model. Latent diffusion and cross-attention are established (R1); related sparse MRI reconstruction is documented in R2. Scanner acceleration and diagnostic use are proposed applications requiring separate evidence.
3:
Sparse-to-dense MRI; missing-slice synthesis; through-plane super-resolution; conditional latent diffusion; neighboring-slice conditioning; Fourier depth embedding; hybrid spatial/cross-attention conditioning; denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM); acquired-slice preservation; volume interpolation; intensity calibration.
PSNR: peak signal-to-noise ratio. SSIM: structural similarity index measure. MSE: mean squared error. EMA: exponential moving average. HDF5: Hierarchical Data Format version 5. NIfTI: Neuroimaging Informatics Technology Initiative. TRL: technology readiness level.
4:
Present methods include nearest/linear/cubic interpolation, learned slice synthesis, latent diffusion (R1/R2), and approaches addressing inter-slice stochasticity (R3). Commercial AI reconstruction such as Deep Resolve (R8) also exists. Classical interpolation is inexpensive but limited by sampled anatomy; learned priors can generate plausible unsupported detail. The implemented system has no k-space/sinogram measurement model, explicit 3D consistency loss, calibrated uncertainty or clinical validation.
The implemented learned models are two-dimensional; stacking generated planes creates a volume. No three-dimensional VAE/U-Net or CNN/ViT backbone choice is implemented.
5: R1 establishes latent diffusion and cross-attention; R2 addresses sparse cardiac MRI reconstruction and is a close conceptual overlap; R3 addresses inter-slice noise correlation; R4 discloses recursive missing-slice interpolation. R5 full description and claims 1-11 were retrieved during this revision; section 21 provides the comparison and retrieval limitations. Additional screening: R17 addresses thick-slice lumbar reconstruction with a latent diffusion prior; R18 addresses undersampled MRI with an MRI VAE and latent diffusion prior. These applications reinforce that latent diffusion in medical reconstruction is established. No head-to-head performance comparison was conducted.

Input: a registered depth-first stack (D,C,H,W) and unique acquired depth indices including both boundaries. Validate channels, dimensions, finite values and checkpoints. Derive 0.5th/99.5th percentile foreground intensity bounds only from acquired slices; apply the same clipping/scaling to context and targets. For each missing depth locate bounding acquired slices and calculate z/(D-1), alpha and gap/16. Encode context, seed a Gaussian latent, predict noise through 25 or 50 DDIM updates, decode and assign the generated slice. Optionally apply Gaussian smoothing (sigma 0.5 along depth) and restore original acquired values. Export a research NIfTI/HDF5 volume with normalization, seed and checkpoint provenance; evaluate against withheld targets only when available.
Exact preservation applies to the supplied normalized acquired planes restored after optional smoothing. Percentile clipping is not invertible preservation of raw scanner intensities, and preservation of acquired planes is not evidence that synthesized planes are anatomically correct.

A computer-implemented research system reconstructs missing axial brain MRI slices from sparse acquired slices. A shared residual convolutional encoder processes the bounding slices. Three-coordinate Fourier embeddings encode normalized depth, relative position and slice gap. Spatial context and cross-attention tokens condition a latent denoising U-Net; DDIM sampling and a pretrained VAE decoder generate missing slices. Assembly optionally smooths along depth and restores acquired slices exactly.
Input: a registered depth-first stack (D,C,H,W) and unique acquired depth indices including both boundaries. Validate channels, dimensions, finite values and checkpoints. For each missing depth locate bounding acquired slices and calculate z/(D-1), alpha and gap/16. Encode context, seed a Gaussian latent, predict noise through 25 or 50 DDIM updates, decode and assign the generated slice. Optionally apply Gaussian smoothing (sigma 0.5 along depth) and restore original acquired values. Working example: D=155, C=1, H=W=240. At stride 8, acquired indices include 0,8,...,152,154 (21 acquired and 134 missing); at stride 16 they include 0,16,...,144,154 (11 acquired and 144 missing). A target at z=12 bounded by z=8 and z=16 has alpha=0.5, depth=12/154 and normalized gap=0.5. Context is computed only from those acquired slices. The trained VAE maps a 240x240 image to four 30x30 latent channels: 8x spatial downsampling per axis and 16x scalar-element reduction for FLAIR. Code path and results are supplied in sections 15-17.

Coordinates: alpha=(z-z_prev)/(z_next-z_prev), depth=z/(D-1), gap=(z_next-z_prev)/16. Normalization: I_norm=2*(clip(I,vmin,vmax)-vmin)/(vmax-vmin+epsilon)-1, with background mapped to -1 and epsilon=1e-7. Clean latent: z0=0.18215*(mu+sigma*epsilon). Forward diffusion: z_t=sqrt(alpha_bar_t)*z0+sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)*epsilon. Noise objective: E[||epsilon-epsilon_theta(z_t,t,context)||^2]. Deterministic DDIM: predicted z0=(z_t-sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)*epsilon_theta)/sqrt(alpha_bar_t); z_prev=sqrt(alpha_bar_prev)*predicted z0+sqrt(1-alpha_bar_prev)*epsilon_theta. VAE objective: L1+0.5*MSE+1e-5*KL+0.1*spatial-gradient L1. Reconstruction MSE=mean((prediction-target)^2); MAE=mean(abs(prediction-target)); PSNR=10*log10(4/MSE) for [-1,1], capped at 100 dB for near-perfect matches. SSIM uses an 11x11 Gaussian window (sigma 1.5), constants (0.01*2)^2 and (0.03*2)^2, averaged over 2D slices/channels.
